title.en: AI Assurance, Red Teaming and Governance for Engineering Leads
title.ar: ضمان أنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي وتمارين الفرق الحمراء والحوكمة لقادة الفرق الهندسية

tagline: Plan and run a bilingual red-team exercise, assess the risk with the national framework, review the architecture and brief the accountable executive on what remains
description: Participants lead the assurance of AI systems that act on an organisation's data. For the fictional Northern Region Benefits Agency (a bilingual benefits assistant and a case-worker agent that reads case files and drafts letters) they plan and run a red-team exercise in Arabic and English, manually and with automated probes, assess the risks with the National AI Risk Management Framework, review the security architecture for agent identity, least privilege, isolation and egress, and assemble an assurance case that ends in a residual-risk briefing. Targets run in a sandbox on synthetic case data. Hardening a single application is AE-308.
audience: Specialists. Engineers who have completed the level 300 core and the practicum, or can show equivalent work: an AI system they built, operated and defended in review.
prerequisites: AE-308 Securing Language Model and Agent Applications
AE-303 Evaluation-Driven Development for Language Model Applications
Has written a threat model for a system they built
Reads a risk register and a likelihood and impact matrix

outcomes.text: Plan a red-team exercise with objectives tied to harms, scope, rules of engagement and stop conditions, given a benefits assistant and a tool-using agent with their intended uses
outcomes.evidence: a test plan that a reviewer approves against a planning checklist

outcomes.text: Conduct manual and automated adversarial testing in Arabic and English and quantify attack success over repeated trials, given sandboxed targets, technique catalogues and a fixed budget of model calls
outcomes.evidence: attack logs, a findings report with success rates, intervals and severity, and three regression tests

outcomes.text: Assess the risks of an agent with the national framework, from context to treatment and residual sign-off, given the agent's design, its supplier contract and a control library
outcomes.evidence: a risk register with calibrated 4 by 4 scores, treatments, residual scores and named owners

outcomes.text: Review a security architecture for agent identity, delegated authority, least privilege, isolation and egress control, given the agent's design documents and three delegation chains
outcomes.evidence: a review report with findings, severity and decision records for the proposed fixes

outcomes.text: Build an assurance case that links each claim to evidence and maps the evidence to a control framework, given the test, risk and review outputs and a control framework
outcomes.evidence: an assurance case diagram and a gap list an auditor would accept as complete

outcomes.text: Present residual risk and a recommendation with conditions to an accountable executive, given the assurance pack and a scripted supplier model change
outcomes.evidence: a one-page residual-risk statement and a briefing scored by the panel

case_study.name: Northern Region Benefits Agency
case_study.summary: A fictional regional agency that pays family, disability and housing benefits. Its assurance team, led by Sulafa Al-Nashmi, examines two systems before the deputy governor signs for them: Mueen, the bilingual benefits assistant, and Katib, the case-worker agent that reads case files and drafts letters. Both run in a sandbox on 300 synthetic case files written with a fixed seed; no real person, case or address is described.

format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

days.title: Plan the exercise

sessions.title: Assurance is an argument with evidence
outcomes: State a top claim that evidence could show to be false
Separate a claim, its argument and its evidence
Name the evidence that defeats a claim and who is independent enough to produce it

lab.title: A top claim and its defeaters
lab.summary: Write the top claim for the benefits assistant and list evidence that would support or defeat it

steps.text: Read the intended use and the system card of Mueen
Write the top claim and three sub-claims
List supporting and defeating evidence for each sub-claim
Mark who may produce each item: the builder or an independent tester

lab.stretch: Write the top claim for Katib and say which sub-claim has no counterpart in Mueen

sessions.summary: Why a test result means nothing until it is tied to a claim, and which evidence would defeat that claim

sessions.title: Scoping from the threat model
outcomes: Read a threat model as a list of testable paths
Find the paths where private data, untrusted content and an exit path meet
Rank paths for testing by harm and by how little the attacker needs

lab.title: Missing paths in the threat model
lab.summary: Review the agent's provided threat model, add missing paths where private data, untrusted content and an exit path meet, and rank them for testing

steps.text: Read the provided threat model and the tool list of Katib
Tag every tool and store: private data, untrusted content, exit
Find the paths where the three meet and add the missing ones
Rank the paths for testing

lab.stretch: Find a path that needs two case files and say why a single-file test would miss it

sessions.summary: How a threat model becomes the scope of a test: the paths where private data, untrusted content and an exit meet

sessions.title: Objectives, scope and rules of engagement
outcomes: Write objectives that name a harm and a way to decide success
Set scope, rules of engagement and a budget of model calls
Write stop conditions and a procedure for harmful outputs

lab.title: A test plan a reviewer approves
lab.summary: Write a test plan with objectives tied to harms, stop conditions and handling of harmful outputs

steps.text: Write four objectives, each tied to a harm and a success check
Set the scope, what is out of scope and the call budget
Write the stop conditions and the harmful-output procedure
Run the planning checklist and fix what it rejects

lab.stretch: Add the rules for an attacker model: what it may generate, where its outputs are kept and who reads them

sessions.summary: What a test plan must say before the first probe is sent: objectives, scope, rules of engagement, stop conditions

sessions.title: Choosing techniques from catalogues
outcomes: Map a planned attack to an OWASP entry and a MITRE ATLAS technique
Tie every attack to a plan objective and drop those that serve none
Read coverage both ways: objectives without attacks and entries without tests

lab.title: Ten attacks, mapped and pruned
lab.summary: Map ten planned attacks to OWASP and ATLAS entries and drop two that serve no objective

steps.text: Read the ten planned attacks and the catalogue extract
Map each attack to an OWASP entry and an ATLAS technique
Tie each attack to an objective and drop the two that serve none
Read the coverage table: which objective has too few attacks

lab.stretch: Write one new attack for an agentic entry that no planned attack covers

sessions.summary: How technique catalogues turn objectives into a list of attacks, and how to drop the attacks that serve none

days.subtitle: From the top claim to a test plan a reviewer approves

days.title: Run the red team

sessions.title: Manual probing in two languages
outcomes: Probe a target by hand and log every attempt, failed ones included
Carry one attack across English, Arabic and transliterated Arabic
Decide success from what happened, not from what the model said

lab.title: Three scripts, one log
lab.summary: Attack the assistant in English, Arabic and transliterated Arabic and log every attempt

steps.text: Write five probes in English and send each once
Rewrite them in Arabic and in transliterated Arabic
Send every probe five times and log every attempt
Compare success by script and write two observations

lab.stretch: Add a Gulf-dialect version of your best probe and compare it with the Modern Standard Arabic one

sessions.summary: Probing by hand in English, Arabic and transliterated Arabic, with a log that someone else can replay

sessions.title: Indirect injection and goal hijack
outcomes: Plant an instruction in content the agent reads as part of its task
Tell a goal hijack from a data exfiltration by the evidence each leaves
Decide success from the exit log of the sandbox

lab.title: A planted line in a case file
lab.summary: Plant an instruction in a case file and try to make the agent send data out of the sandbox

steps.text: Run Katib on a clean case file and read the trace
Plant an instruction in the applicant statement
Decide success from the exit log of the sandbox
Ten trials each for two exits, with rates and intervals

lab.stretch: Hijack the goal without any exit: make Katib write a false approval note in the case file

sessions.summary: Instructions that arrive inside a case file: how an agent is hijacked through its own task, and how to prove data left

sessions.title: Automated campaigns over repeated trials
outcomes: Plan a campaign that fits a fixed budget of model calls
Report attack success as a rate with an interval over repeated trials
Say which differences between techniques and scripts the intervals support

lab.title: A campaign within a budget
lab.summary: Run an automated probing campaign and report attack success with intervals

steps.text: Load the probe set and plan the trials within 600 calls
Run the campaign and keep the log
Compute success rates with intervals by technique and by script
Say which differences the intervals support

lab.stretch: Let the scripted attacker rewrite the three weakest probes and measure whether the rewrite helps

sessions.summary: From single attempts to a campaign: trials, a call budget, success rates with intervals

sessions.title: Findings people can act on
outcomes: Rate a finding for severity, likelihood and reproducibility from its evidence
Write a finding with the steps, the rate and the affected claim
Turn a finding into a regression test with a threshold over trials

lab.title: Three findings, one regression test
lab.summary: Rate three provided findings for severity, likelihood and reproducibility and turn one into a regression test

steps.text: Rate three findings for severity and likelihood
Replay each finding from its log and rate reproducibility
Write one finding in the report shape
Turn it into a regression test with a threshold

lab.stretch: Run your regression test against the scripted model change and explain the result

sessions.summary: What turns an attack log into a finding an owner can fix, and a finding into a test that keeps it fixed

days.title: Assess the risk

sessions.title: The national framework as method

Record context and scope: system and use limits, data and parties, automation and the human role, life cycle and change
Separate intended uses from uses that are out of scope

lab.summary: Set context, scope and stakeholders for the case-worker agent using the framework's phases

steps.text: Describe the system, its intended uses and the uses out of scope
List the data, the entry and exit points and the parties
State the level of automation and the human decision points

lab.stretch: Name the reference pillar that each of your out-of-scope uses rests on

sessions.summary: The National AI Risk Management Framework as a working method: its steps, and what context and scope must record

sessions.title: Scoring and calibration
outcomes: Classify a risk into the seven types of the national framework
Score likelihood and impact from stated evidence on the 4 by 4 matrix
Calibrate with a second scorer and record the reason for every changed score

lab.title: Twelve risks, two scorers
lab.summary: Score twelve risks alone on the 4 by 4 matrix, then calibrate with a partner

steps.text: Classify twelve risks into the seven types
Score likelihood and impact alone
Compare with the partner sheet and find the gaps
Calibrate on evidence and record the agreed scores

lab.stretch: Compute the weighted agreement before and after calibration

sessions.summary: Scoring likelihood and impact on the national 4 by 4 matrix, and calibrating two scorers on evidence

sessions.title: Treatment and residual risk
outcomes: Choose among avoid, mitigate, transfer and accept with a reason
Re-score residual likelihood and impact from what a control changes
Name the owner, the signatory and the review date of every residual risk

lab.title: Treat the top three
lab.summary: Choose controls for the three highest risks in a provided register and state residual scores and signatories

steps.text: Rank the register and take the three highest risks
Choose a strategy and controls from the control library
Re-score residual likelihood and impact with a reason
Name the owner, the signatory and the review date

lab.stretch: Find the risk in the register that should be avoided, not mitigated, and say what is switched off

sessions.summary: Choosing a treatment, re-scoring what remains and getting a named person to sign for it

sessions.title: Supplier and model-change risk
outcomes: Read a model update notice against the supplier contract
Decide which risks and which tests a model change reopens
Give a go, a go with conditions or a hold, with the evidence each needs

lab.title: A model update notice
lab.summary: Assess a supplier's model update notice and decide what must be retested before it goes live

steps.text: Read the update notice against the contract clauses
Classify the change and name the risks it reopens
Choose what must be retested from the regression suite
Decide: go, go with conditions or hold

lab.stretch: Run the regression suite against the changed model and compare it with your retest choice

sessions.summary: What a supplier may change without asking, and how a model update notice becomes a retest decision
